# Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII): agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-27, research snapshot `eb0f129dc54e`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Brief version: rules, recovery, bugs, incidents and open questions. The full pack [analog-rytm.md](analog-rytm.md) adds all facts.

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc] [hw]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [doc] [emu] [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [emu] [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [emu] [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]
- **A65** Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost. [hw]
- **A66** On a DSP that waits on a second core, put long work at the end of the frame, not at its head. [hw]
- **A67** Never raise a note's trig and its end in the same audio block. [hw]
- **A68** Before a software reset, anything the next boot must read has to be in RAM, not only in the cache. [hw]
- **A69** Take the stock bytes a run-time patch replays from a copy made before the OS and the flashed build ran, never from live RAM. [emu]
- **A70** Never land a change on the tick a stock event is due and rely on a tie between its time and the clock. [hw]
- **A71** Write at most one value per track, step and parameter in one change. [emu]
- **A72** When you extend a stock table that a setting indexes, extend every table that setting indexes, including tables the OS builds in RAM at run time. [hw]
- **A73** A neutral setting of an effect must give back stock's routing, not only a flat response. [hw]
- **A74** Build mod code with undefined-behaviour warnings as errors, at least `-Werror=return-type`. [emu]
- **A75** On the Model:Cycles, an added machine whose oscillator runs on through a trig must keep the stock VCA from cutting at the trig. [hw]
- **A76** Syntakt: never write SPI NOR `0x300000-0x380000`, and keep the OS container under 2 MB. [doc]
- **A77** Before you store mod data in a byte of a stock record, find every stock routine that reads or writes it, and test with a project that uses every feature of that record. [hw]
- **A78** When a base keeps its own data inside a stock record, shrink the core's area by the same bytes and refuse an overlap at build time. [hw]
- **A79** Test every edit path on a pattern, bank and project far from the defaults, not only on A01. [hw]
- **A80** A parameter a mod sets right before it plays a note may be smoothed by the OS: set the smoothing state too, or set the value a few blocks earlier, and listen on a unit. [hw]
- **A81** A sound a mod starts without a trig must obey the track's mute itself. [?]
- **A82** On the Octatrack, read the Part a track is playing from stock's per-track pair (`0x8000182a` / `0x80001832` + t), not from the UI or engine Part. [hw]
- **A83** Test the smallest legal build as well as the full one. [hw]
- **A84** When you patch a stock routine for audio tracks, find its MIDI-track twin and patch and test that too. [hw]
- **A85** A mod machine that stock sees as another machine must handle both edges of a machine switch itself. [hw]
- **A86** Take key ids from the target device's own decoder table, never from another model. [emu] [hw]
- **A87** Place card data by the smallest capacity the firmware accepts, and check the capacity the driver reports before you touch the card. [hw]
- **A88** When a mod changes the USB descriptors at run time, bring the controller back from a context that keeps running, check that it attached, and keep every other host client off the device while it reconnects. [hw]
- **A89** On the Octatrack, do not change which effects the DSP holds while a project loads; plan only from the complete effect map. [hw]
- **A90** Load from the card only when a sound needs it, never on every knob or modulation step. [hw]
- **A91** Rewrite a playing track only behind the playhead, and expect the change on the next loop. [emu] [hw]
- **A92** Before you bring a dormant stock routine or buffer into use, find what else uses that memory. [doc]
- **A93** A USB Audio layout must run on the host's own class driver before you ship it. [hw]
- **A94** Do not gate a feature on a one-time handshake sent at link-up; re-detect the peer from ongoing traffic. [doc]
- **A95** Data a saved pattern or project points to must not change after the save; act on a stock reload only once the stock has accepted it. [hw]
- **A96** Check every precondition of a RAM boot before anything is uploaded, and count every restart against a pending update. [hw]
- **A97** Keep a stock UI widget inside the range stock gives it. [hw]
- **A98** Draw only from the task that owns the screen; from a tick or a higher-priority task, post a request instead. [hw]
- **A99** When you add rows, questions or pages to stock UI, redraw them yourself and use stock's own windows for questions. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII)

- **A104** (B) When a mod turns an input stock ignores into one it acts on, also post every event stock pairs with it. The Rytm's panel driver posts a pad release only after a real strike; Light Taps turned a light tap into a soft hit and, without a release, a retrig roll kept running ([I239](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i239-a-light-tap-with-retrig-kept-its-roll-running-light-taps-analog-rytm-mkii)). `[hw]` {modwerk-1127}
- **D6** (D) Custom machine IDs are permanent once kits store them. Range 4-127. Claim `machine:<id>`. Known claims (Digitakt mk1, core 2.1): 4 = NEIGHBOR, 5 = DIGISLICER. Pick a free ID, then register it in [`devices/digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} D6b. Digitone II machine IDs: synths 5-31 and filters 6-31 are separate namespaces, permanent, and there is no allocator - agree IDs with other authors before shipping; saved sounds of an absent mod keep their ID and show as MISSING. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2} D6c. Analog Rytm MKII mod machines take the hidden slots 34-43 (from elekloader core-ar2 0.13 also the TEST slots 44-52), claimed as `machine:<slot>`. Kits store the slot; on a build without the mod the kit loads it as DISABLE. elekloader refuses two mods with the same slot, and Modwerk also records claims on its agent board. Each slot has fixed knob positions, so give meaning to a sound index, not to a knob letter. `[doc]` {modwerk-rytm-machines}
- **D10** (D) Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building} (`recovery#ff8f0917`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L37))

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB18** Edits to hidden FX words overwrite the delay's saved TIME (latent) (Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74; stock behaviour). Workaround: keep mod values for those words in your own storage (Modwerk's base redirects them to its kit storage).
- **SB19** A non-sample file on the +Drive hangs LOAD TO PROJECT and later stalls the OS upgrade (Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74; stock behaviour). Workaround: a tool that stores other files on the +Drive starts each with 16 zero bytes, which stock loads as an empty sample (elekloader's Drive Loader does this).
- **SB21** The Rytm MKI's in-OS upgrade decodes into a 2 MiB buffer without a bound check (Analog Rytm MKI, OS 1.74; open in stock). Workaround: keep an image at or below `0x1F0000` bytes (elekloader's limit).
- **SB25** FX-track lock indexes 38-41 read past their table and share rows with 18-21 (Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74; open; seen in the emulator only.). Workaround: a mod that writes FX-track locks should treat 38-41 and 18-21 as one row each.
- **SB27** The UI queue overwrites unread messages when more than 1024 wait (Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74; stock behaviour). Workaround: keep audio-block load low enough that the UI task keeps up; a mod that posts to the queue keeps its own bounded pool and counts only its own waiting events.
- **SB28** Data transfer progress wraps for files over 4,294,967 bytes (Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74; open). Workaround: a client counts the bytes it gets; elekloader's tools do.
- **SB36** Pad pressure goes to the wrong note in CHROMATIC mode and is dropped during RTRG rolls (Rytm MKII) (Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74; open in stock). Workaround: Modwerk's Pad Pressure Fix module (0.2.0-experimental) sends pressure on the played note and routes roll pressure to aftertouch and MIDI out; its fixes are moving into the Modwerk Rytm base.

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I131** An overloaded Rytm overwrote its own UI messages and lost live-recorded hits. Cause: stock's UI queue send has no full check, so past 1024 waiting messages it overwrites unread ones (pad pressure, keys, a mod's events). The load (BD ANALOG voices, stock pad pressure at 200-290 messages a second) was past what the UI task can serve. Fix: none in stock. Live Rec Retrig Fix 0.2.2 frees its slots only after the UI task has taken its message, and drops only its own events past 126 waiting; with lighter load (LQ04, BD ANALOG alone) 145 hits, 0 dropped. Rules: A50.
- **I49** Idle paths of sixteen mods cost two percent of a Rytm block. Cause: three modules did work every block with nothing to do: Ping Pong Loop's four voice gates called the mirror routine for every voice in stock's sample prefetch, Sample Playback Rate walked all eight voices, QPERF ran its handler in full. Fix: early returns when idle (a byte of armed voices, "no track has RATE on"): 70.6-71.1 %. Rules: A34.
- **I55** A knob's own push-button byte was read as FUNC. Cause: the module took byte +20 of the encoder event as FUNC; that byte is set while the knob's own push-button is held. Fix: build MBC3 reads FUNC from the stock key table. Rules: C10.
- **I97** Four software drum voices overran an Analog Rytm's audio block. Cause: the stock block already takes about two thirds of its time, and the unit costs about three times the emulator's instruction count (EMAC latency, cache refills). Fix: voices hand-scheduled in assembly; BD ANALOG offered on three tracks only. Rules: A34.
- **I99** The first note after a RAM load was near silent on a Rytm. Cause: a boot from flash was not tried. Fix: waiting 3 s before the first note (0 of 7). Rules: A40.
- **I111** A mod's own SysEx report cut a stock pattern dump on an Analog Rytm. Cause: a stock multi-part dump releases the MIDI lock between its parts while its SysEx state at `0x413db244` stays set; the mod's try-send took the lock in such a gap and put its own message inside the dump. Fix: 0.5.0 sends only while `0x413db244` is zero, checked before the try-lock and again while holding the lock, with the wait bounded at 2 s. Rules: F8.
- **I127** YES changed a track at once with RECORD off (trig-seedr 0.5.0, Analog Rytm MKII). Cause: the mod must write stored trigs to be heard (stock's Euclidean mode plays a separate pattern and never touches stored trigs), and 0.5.0 treated leaving as keeping. Fix: 0.5.1 "generate and apply": YES writes only with grid recording on (flag byte `0x417e320c`), FUNC + YES is the only way a take stays, and changing track or pattern, closing or turning RECORD off restores the original (NOT APPLIED). 0.6.0 played on the unit: works. 0.7.0 adds a pending-take dot and makes YES after a revert bring the same take back. Rules: C11.
- **I132** A rate mod silenced the Rytm's sample preview. Cause: stock's preview routine `0x400a0dac` puts the sample in slot 129 with TUN and FIN at rest (`0x4000`); the mod read FIN at rest as RATE 0 and scaled the step to 0. Fix: 0.5.1 plays any voice whose sample slot is 128 or above at 1x, forward. The author's unit (SU02, from RAM): previews at RATE 0, +63, -64 and with an LFO on RATE all at normal speed. Rules: C11.
- **I151** A Rytm MKII mod read a 32-bit kit index as 16 bits and played the old sound (MIDI Engine). Cause: the current kit's index is a 32-bit word; the build read its top half, which is 0, so it always used kit 1. Fix: read the whole word (ME09); reproduced and cleared in rytm-emu with kit 2 current. Rules: A51.
- **I40** A "no change" rebuild came out 2 bytes short. Cause: elektron-firmware-tool padded ELE2 containers to 2 bytes; stock pads to 4. Fix: pad to 4; always null-repack the stock file first. Rules: A6,A32.
- **I56** A test plan pressed the wrong key, and the emulator reference did not match the unit. Cause: rytm2_mods' documentation gives the reload key as NO + PLAY, so the remote-key plan pressed transport PLAY; the OS 1.74 manual says NO + PLAY MODE. Fix: rerun with NO + PLAY MODE and narrow the screen check to the cursor row. Rules: C8,C10.
- **I98** MIDI hits on a software voice were silent on a Rytm; the emulator could not show it. Cause: a MIDI trig sets the voice timer to a start tick of 0-15 or later, but the base took a hit only when it read 0; rytm-emu does not trigger track 1 from pads or MIDI, so only sequencer trigs had been tested. Fix: the voice waits for the scheduled tick, as stock BD CLASSIC does (`0x40110a06`). Rules: C10.
- **I112** The compiler merged two stores and broke a step move (trig-seedr, emulator). Cause: Homebrew m68k-elf-gcc 16.2 at -O2 miscompiled a struct copy followed by stores to its fields; with store merging one 4-byte store landed 6 bytes early. Fix: from 0.4.1 every ColdFire build (the mod, core-ar2, the device checks) uses `-fno-store-merging`. 0.4.0 had passed every emulator check, so the same fault may sit in code the checks do not reach. Rules: A41.
- **I126** Two lock lanes on one parameter lost one lane's locks (trig-seedr, emulator). Cause: the Rytm keeps one lock per parameter and step; the second write replaced the first. Fix: 0.6.0 refuses such a recipe (SETTING OUT OF RANGE, nothing written) and LOCK's PARM skips the other lane's parameter; host test `test_found_lanes`. Rules: A71.
- **I128** Idle CPU cost overstated five times: an instruction budget read as one second (trig-seedr, analog-emu). Cause: `dtboot --instr 1000M` at the default `--ips 200M` runs 5 emulated seconds; the count was divided by one second. Fix: measured again per emulated second: 1.9 %, then 0.25 % after redrawing only on change; F10's status file carries a correction. Rules: C10.
- **I142** A function without a return value passed the emulator by chance (trig-seedr 0.7.0). Cause: undefined return value in C (m68k-elf-gcc gives no error by default); the register happened to hold a non-zero value in the emulator runs. Fix: `return 1;` added; the mod builds with `-Werror=return-type`. Rules: A74.
- **I102** A repacked stock image ran on an Analog Rytm MKI, and stock came back over USB and DIN. Cause: a null repack before any mod, the first check of a new file writer. Fix: none needed. Rules: A2,A6.
- **I152** A Transfer install stalled at "Waiting for SysEx" on a Rytm MKII. Cause: unknown. Fix: power cycle and send again. Rules: A23.
- **I186** A user machine that loaded samples between hits reset a Sidecar Pi 5 (WAVESURFER 1.0.0). Cause: in 1.0.0 every knob change asked the Sidecar for the selected sample, so a modulated knob made it load several samples a second from the SD card; long, heavy card reads are the common factor. The Sidecar side of the reset is not explained. Fix: WAVESURFER 1.0.1 asks for a sample only when a trig comes in (or for the one playing); the README asks for samples under 12 MB and 60 s. Rules: A90.
- **I195** Stock Rytm samples played under Sidecar machines (Rytm firmware 0.4.4/0.5.0). Cause: page 2 of every Sidecar machine is the sound's sample words 17-24, and the stock sample player renders them for every voice. The mod zeroed the voice's sample gain (`0x80007000 + 8 x voice`), which scales buffer B only. The layer's output S (`0x800067f8 + 128 x voice`) is written by `sample_render` after the machine renders, so the machine cannot clear it. Fix: Rytm firmware 0.5.1.1: a detour at the mixer call zeroes S of voices under a Sidecar machine, and the stock sample player skips its resampler and filter for those voices (also some Rytm CPU back). A stock track's sample-only trig on a shared voice still plays. The mirror case (a stock-latched engine and a sample-only trig from the Sidecar track) still plays the Rytm sample. Rules: A85,A59.
- **I210** Sidecar features that wait for the Rytm's hello stayed off when the Pi started later. Cause: the modded Rytm sends its hello only when its USB port comes up; a Pi that starts or updates later never hears it. Fix: 0.5.1.2 claims FILL on the first Rytm message and again about every 2 s; a hello, if one comes, still decides. Rules: A94.
- **I239** A light tap with retrig kept its roll running (Light Taps, Analog Rytm MKII). Cause: the panel driver posts a pad release only after a real strike, and a light tap has none, so the module's soft hit was never released. Fix: LT06 posts the release itself when the pad is let go. Rules: A104.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O16** What section 8 is for: A) the Outbox 8 accessory (dnfw: the image arrived in the DN2 release that added Outbox support; an inference from timing) B) the panel MCU firmware (analog-emu)
- **O8** DT2/DN2 NOR flash geometry: A) bootstrap: 512-byte pages, 256 KB erase B) in-OS writer: 0x100-byte pages, 0x10000 sectors from `0x80000`
- **O14** Analog Rytm MKII CPU: A) rytm-fw-re: MCF5445x (`-mcpu=54455`) B) analog-emu and analog-rytm-mkii-research: MCF5441x (same entry code, CACR/ACR and peripheral blocks as the A4 MKII)
- **O29** CRC of a block in stock's 0x51 OS upgrade write: A) common/os-update-protocol.md (DT2/DN2): zlib `crc32(data)` B) Modwerk LINK.md (Analog Rytm MKII): zlib crc32 seeded with 0xffffffff {modwerk-rytm-link}

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H26** (stock) On a stock Analog Rytm MKII (OS 1.74) the first note right after a boot can be silent. Test: Power the stock unit on, wait for the main screen, play one pad or trig once and note whether it sounds; repeat over ten boots.
- **H34** (stock) On Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74 the OS version field of a flashed build shows only on the boot screen; no GLOBAL menu shows it (trig-seedr's corrected check 1). Test: Boot a stock 1.74 unit, look through GLOBAL > SYSTEM for an OS INFO entry; note what the boot screen shows.
- **H36** (stock) The Rytm MKI boot-flash writers lie at `0x40096A6C-0x40096B3E` and BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE ends at `0x4011AA7A` in OS 1.74; the upgrade buffer is `0x40366570` (2 MiB; SB21). Test: Static: disassemble the stock MKI 1.74 image at those addresses and check the callers of the erase and program routines. No flashing needed.
- **H49** (stock) On a Rytm MKII (OS 1.74), Transfer's progress bar goes wrong while reading a file over 4,294,967 bytes from the unit (SB28). Test: Read a sample larger than 4.3 MB back from the unit with Transfer and watch the progress.
- **H52** (stock) On stock Rytm MKII 1.74, TRK SEND MIDI sends only a step's first message on time; later notes of the same step leave 5-30 ms late, more on p-locked steps. Test: Stock OS: TRK SEND MIDI on BD and SD, trigs on the same steps, one p-lock on BD; record DIN out on a computer MIDI monitor and compare each note's time to the step grid.
- **H62** (probe) A stock Analog Rytm MKII (OS 1.74) spends CPU on silence until a power cycle: from a slot's first SYN trig the render calls that slot's machine every block whether it sounds or not (no idle test at `0x40121208`), and delay and reverb once used never decay to exact zero and run at full cost with every send at 0. STOP, a kit load or a project load do not clear it. Test: Read the render load with a probe at boot, after triggering all eight voices once, after one delay and reverb use, after STOP and after a kit reload. Does it stay up until a power cycle?
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).
